newsitem.title: UK: Cambridge Antibody on course in key trials.
newsitem.headline: Cambridge Antibody on course in key trials.

text.p: The newly-listed biotechnology firm, Cambridge Antibody, said on Tuesday that it was confident of sticking to its timetable for starting certain key trials which were crucial to its future growth.
Cambridge said in a statement it would start clinical trials on the anti TGF2 antibody, which combats opthalmic fibrosis, by the end of 1997.

The company said the potential of this antibody to reduce scarring in the central nervous systen was confirmed recently in a fibrosis meeting by its collaborator, Dr Ann Logan, from the University of Birmingham.

Cambridge will commence clinical trials on its tumour necrosis therapy programme in 1998. The company is jointly developing this chimaeric antibody -- for local administration to solid tumours -- with Techniclone Corp.
The company, which got listed on the London Stock Exchange last March, reported a net loss of 6.41 million stg in the six months to March 31, 1997.
